current_scores.prior_score_assessment: No distinct 'prior' AIBQ composite is on record for Perplexity. Per AIBQ v3.0 Principle 8 (carry-forward: scores persist between events, no interpolation), the 3.85 composite dated 2026-05-12 is the only canonical AIBQ entry found and it is still the figure served by the framework/companies page as fetched 2026-08-11 -- i.e. it has apparently not moved in 3 months of coverage. The shared AIBQ Score Tracker (77-row daily-change audit log) has zero rows for Perplexity; that granular change log only covers the Frontier Five, consistent with Perplexity's lighter 'AI Ecosystem' coverage tier (biweekly monitoring).
current_scores.conflict_flag: OPEN CONFLICT: two other 'Unicorn Scores' rows exist for Perplexity, both dated 2026-05-13 (the day after the canonical AIBQ entry), scored under a DIFFERENT framework: PBQ composite 6.30 (CE 7, RQ 5.5, SV 7, GO 6, MD 5, High confidence) and an unlabeled-framework composite 5.95 (CE 3, RQ 7, GO 3, MD 4, High confidence, no CI/SV given). Both are materially higher and structurally different (PBQ substitutes Strategic Velocity for Compute Independence) from the 3.85 AIBQ figure that the canonical company page still serves. Per the framework's own four-question AIBQ-vs-PBQ test, Perplexity's classification is genuinely ambiguous (does not clearly train its own >10B-parameter foundation models; does rely on model access + retrieval for differentiation) -- this may explain why analysts tried it under both rubrics. Not resolved here; both readings are preserved verbatim above.
